about: M4 rule rows. One game-neutral table of combat rules as data. Every row carries a source key naming the donor game or the measured clip. All numbers are START VALUES from donor games, to be measured on our Mixamo and Hellish Quart attack clips before any threshold is final (BRIEF: template layer only). A missing donor number is null with a todo key. Armour only ever raises a dismember threshold and cuts damage; no key in this file may block, prevent or make anything immune (the lint rejects it). Strategy+Dom 2026-10-27: damage is cumulative, zero is dead, light or heavy; no floor; a light never instantly cuts a healthy part; light counter-hit damage is a data row (evaluator.kill.light_damage_mult).

global.source: TABG PlayerDeath.globalDmgMultiplier 0.65 (opentrident-steam docs/parts-lab/combat-physics-comparison-five-games.md section 2.2; COMBAT-101 B5). One row to tune all damage.

strength_scale.formula: tip_speed = hand_speed * lever (or a tip speed given directly); strength = tip_speed * sharpness * (heavy_mult if a heavy swing) * (counter_hit_mult if a counter-hit)
strength_scale.measure_note: Rungs are WEAPON TIP speed in m/s at sharpness 1.0 (the baseline blade, baseline_weapon), re-based from the hand-end percentiles of docs/M4-MEASURE.md by the baseline weapon's lever (lever.arm_reach_m and weapons.gm_gladius.length_m: lever 1.992): hand p10 4.01 x 1.992 = 8.0, hand p50 8.27 x 1.992 = 16.5, hand p90 12.18 x 1.992 = 24.3 (docs/M4-CALIBRATION.md). MEASURED: hand speeds (12 swings, one clip set, one body) and arm reach. ASSUMED: the weapon continues the arm axis and the chain turns about the shoulder (lever formula); the weapon length is a donor number (Gladio Mori weapons-physics.csv), not ours. Not measured: Mixamo and Hellish Quart library clips (not readable from the Mac), the special swing class, a real weapon tip (the dump has no weapon axis). 12 swings is a small sample: re-run on more clips and move the rungs to the new percentiles.
strength_scale.source: V3 recorded fight dump docs/ragdoll-fight-poses.json (902 ticks, 60 Hz, Minotaur on the 65 rig, branch docs/ragdoll-poses), hand-end peak speed per swing, 12 swings with pose snaps excluded: hand p10 4.01 / p50 8.27 / p90 12.18 m/s, times the gladius lever 1.992 (arm reach 0.5634 m, length 0.559 m) = 8.0 / 16.5 / 24.3. Replaces the Gladio and Glory start values 20/50/100 (COMBAT-101 A1 and item 17) and the hand-speed rungs 4.0 / 8.3 / 12.2 of the first M4 measurement.

lever.formula: lever = (arm_reach_m + weapon.length_m) / arm_reach_m; tip_speed = hand_speed * lever
lever.source: Arm reach = shoulder pivot to hand end at rest, 0.5634 m, from the V3 Minotaur body (data/bodies/minotaur.measure.json through generateRow and buildDefinition; printed by tools/tip-speed.mjs). Default for a body without its own arm reach: pass hit.armReachM to override per attacker. Lever formula is an ASSUMPTION (the weapon continues the arm and rotates with it about the shoulder; COMBAT-101 A2: tip speed is arm length times angular speed).

swing.todo: counter_hit_mult is an OWN start value (picked so heavy x counter-hit clears the top plate threshold with margin, docs/M4-CALIBRATION.md); measure it on counter-hit clips. heavy_mult is the heavy / light MEDIAN peak hand speed ratio (12.01 / 6.25 = 1.92) of 5 long and 7 short swings, split by run duration, not by a clip label, so re-measure on labelled charged clips; the p90 ratio is only 1.31. heavy_mult stands for the charge; do not also feed the faster hand speed of a heavy animation (counts the heavy twice).
swing.source: heavy_mult: V3 Minotaur fight dump (tools/tip-speed.mjs light and heavy classes, run duration at the 0.2 s median): heavy p50 12.01 m/s over light p50 6.25 m/s. hand_speed_ref_m_s: the same table (docs/M4-MEASURE.md); light_p90 = the full-speed light swing every calibration row uses. counter_hit_mult: own start value (COMBAT-101 core doc: only a heavy or a counter-hit cuts mail and plate).

melee_speed_gate.source: min_speed_m_s 8.0 = p10 of the swing peaks (4.01 m/s hand) x the baseline lever 1.992, in tip speed (same number as rung_hit): 90 percent of our swings pass; TABG's 5 m/s (relativeVelocity >= 5 m/s then num = clamp(v x 2, 0, 1); five-games doc section 2.2; COMBAT-101 B5) is a contact speed with no lever, so it sits near the hand p17. full_strength_margin_m_s 0.5 is still the TABG start value (not measurable from a pose dump).

bone_gate.armour_effect: armour multiplies the gate by its dismember_threshold_modifier (raises it, finite, never a wall)
bone_gate.source: Gladio Mori Blade.CheckBoneBreak: speed^2 x boneMultiplier > 9, so gate = 3 / sqrt(boneMult) m/s; bone multipliers 0.5 to 5 (five-games doc 2.1 and 5). Start shape, UNCHANGED by M4: at numerator 3 the gate (2.7 to 3.0 m/s for bone_mult 1.0 to 1.2) is under 11 to 12 of the 12 measured HAND peaks (min 2.95 m/s) and far under any weapon TIP speed (hand x lever, at least 1.6), so on our clips the cut rung (24.3 m/s of tip speed at sharpness 1) is what binds, not this gate (docs/M4-MEASURE.md, docs/M4-CALIBRATION.md). The gate compares the physical tip speed (not multiplied by heavy or counter-hit). Left for Dom: raise the numerator only if the bone gate should bind.

plate_t3.source: role table armour_tiers (own start values; top plate cut 0.35, threshold 2.5). Design check (docs/M4-CALIBRATION.md): the strongest allowed hit must clear 2.5x the cut rung, or top armour is a block in practice. Threshold 2.5 x 24.3 = 60.75 m/s of strength. Baseline blade, full-speed light hand speed 9.74 m/s: tip 19.4, x heavy_mult 1.92 = 37.3, x counter_hit_mult 1.75 = 65.2 > 60.75 (reachable only with a heavy AND a counter-hit; heavy alone 37.3 cuts up to mail 36.5; light + counter-hit 33.9 does not cut mail). The earlier hand-speed scale had top plate unreachable (30.5 needed vs 13.09 fastest swing); the lever, the heavy swing and per-weapon sharpness (best slash ratio 1.0, so the gain is in the lever and the swing type) fix that. MEASURED: hand speeds. ASSUMED: lever formula, weapon length. OWN: counter_hit_mult 1.75.

fall_seconds.source: TABG RagdollHandler.Fall: damage over 60 falls 0.2 s, push force over 80 falls 0.5 s, downed 2 s (five-games doc 2.2; COMBAT-101 B5)

knockdown.stun_note: diminishing stun: each stun inside the window lasts 100, 50, 25 percent, then 0 (stun-immune window for the stun only; it never touches cut or dismember)
knockdown.source: Separate from the kill budgets (COMBAT-101 A4 and item 16): Gladio cumulative-damage-since-last-fall counter, 60 of 120, resets on each fall; get-up grace 1.5 s and stun diminishing returns 100/50/25 from item 16 (Lost Ark, AzerothCore); recovery 0.3 per second from TABG. Start values.

kill.light_damage_note: OWN start value (Strategy+Dom 2026-10-27: damage is cumulative, zero is dead, light or heavy; NO floor, do not reinstate light_floor_pct or heavy_kill_floor_pct). A LIGHT swing on a kill part (any_part_gone: head, torso) deals strength x zone x global x this multiplier; heavy swings and every limb are unchanged. Cause of 'one light hit, the Minotaur falls': a light counter-hit is 1.75 x a light swing, so its strength (28.7 to 32.4 on a longsword, katana row) is over rung_cut 24.3 and a cut removes the whole part budget; its damage was also ~78% of a Minotaur torso in one blow. A light swing never CUTS a head or torso while the part's hp is above the damage the blow itself deals; once hp <= that damage it kills normally by damage. At 0.4 a fresh Minotaur-scale torso (76) takes 6 to 10 mixed lights or 2 heavies. 1 = the old strength-only damage. No rung moved.
